title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): E is an elliptic curve over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic ≠ 2. Put F_n = Γ(E, O(n·0_E)). Riemann–Roch gives dim F_n = n for n ≥ 1, and F_0 = F_1 = k·1. F_* = ⊕ F_n is the graded section ring of O(0_E), i.e. the Rees algebra of the pole-order filtration, and Proj F_* ≅ E. The leading-polar-coefficient map gives an exact sequence 0 → F_{n-1} → F_n → t_E^{⊗n} → 0 for n ≥ 2. Here t_E is the tangent space at 0, and O(n0)/O((n-1)0) restricted to 0 is (T_0)^{⊗n}. The goal of the whole note is to determine F_* intrinsically: the Weierstrass presentation written coordinate-free in terms of t_E.

This page:
(8) Each δ ∈ t_E extends to a translation-invariant vector field on E. Acting as a derivation, it raises pole order at 0 by exactly one, giving θ_δ : F_n → F_{n+1}. This is a derivation of degree +1 of the graded algebra F_*, and it kills the degree-1 generator 1 ∈ F_1.
(9) θ_δ maps the filtration exact sequence for n to that for n+1. On top-degree symbols it induces t_E^{⊗n} → t_E^{⊗(n+1)}. In a local parameter z, d/dz (z^{-n}) = -n z^{-n-1}, so this map is really -n·(multiplication by δ). Grothendieck writes 'multiplication par δ' and drops the factor -n.
(10) Intrinsic version: δ_n : t_E ⊗ F_n → F_{n+1}, δ ⊗ φ ↦ θ_δ φ.
(11) δ_n is a morphism of exact sequences, with right-hand vertical map t_E ⊗ t_E^{⊗n} → t_E^{⊗(n+1)} claimed to be the canonical isomorphism. By the snake lemma, Ker δ_n = Ker δ_{n-1} for n ≥ 2.
(12) Hence Ker δ_n = Ker δ_1 = t_E ⊗ F_1 = t_E ⊗ k·1_E: only the constants are killed. Also Ker θ_δ = F_1 = k·1_E (for δ ≠ 0).
(13)–(14) The inversion [-1] gives an involution f ↦ f^∨, f^∨(x) = f(-x), of the graded commutative algebra F_*.

The next page shows θ_δ anticommutes with ∨. It splits F_n = F_n^+ ⊕ F_n^- and identifies F_2 = F_2^+ with functions on E/±1 ≅ P^1. This is the start of an intrinsic derivation of the Weierstrass form: x spans F_2 mod constants, y = θ_δ x spans F_3^-, and the derivation structure t_E → Der^{+1}(F_*) is part of the data.
errors: The map on graded pieces induced by θ_δ is not plain multiplication by δ but (-n)·δ (d/dz z^{-n} = -n z^{-n-1}). So in (11) the right-hand vertical arrow is -n times the canonical isomorphism. It is an isomorphism only when n is invertible in k.

Consequently the conclusion (12), Ker δ_n = Ker δ_1 = t_E⊗k·1 and Ker θ_δ = k·1, is valid only in characteristic 0, or in characteristic p for degrees n < p. The hypothesis on this page is only 'char ≠ 2'. In characteristic p ≥ 3, every p-th power f^p (e.g. x^p ∈ F_{2p}) is killed by θ_δ, so Ker θ_δ contains k[T, x^p, y^p, ...] and is much larger than k·1.
In (9) the bottom-right term is written t_E^{⊗n}; it should be t_E^{⊗(n+1)}, as Grothendieck correctly writes in (11).
Minor: the leftmost term of the top row of (9) should be 0 (exactness); the sequences are exact only for n ≥ 2 (resp. n-1 ≥ 1).

ideas.what: Graded section ring ⊕Γ(E,O(n·0)) of an elliptic curve, with the pole-order filtration and symbol maps to t_E^{⊗n}
ideas.modern_name: Section ring / Rees algebra of O(0_E); intrinsic Weierstrass model; modular forms as sections of ω^{⊗k}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass); intrinsic form in Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire' (1975), Katz (1973), Katz–Mazur (1985)

ideas.what: Invariant vector field δ ∈ t_E acting as a degree +1 derivation of the section ring, with symbol map δ ⊗ φ ↦ θ_δ φ
ideas.modern_name: Invariant derivation d/dz acting on Weierstrass functions (x' = y up to constants); derivation-structure on the graded ring
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass ℘, ℘'); standard in Silverman, Deligne formulaire

ideas.what: Involution [-1]^* on F_* and the even/odd decomposition
ideas.modern_name: Action of the inversion; quotient E/±1 ≅ P^1 (Kummer line)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coordinate-free re-derivation of the Weierstrass graded ring and its invariant derivation, standard material (Deligne's formulaire, Katz–Mazur). The only notable feature is a characteristic-p slip: the kernel computation ignores the factor -n, which is not original mathematics.
transcription_corrections: In (9) the symbol transcribed as 'Hδ' is more likely 'μ_δ' (multiplication by δ), consistent with the following sentence.
In (9) the bottom-right entry on the page reads t_E^{⊗n} (Grothendieck's slip; should be ⊗(n+1)).
'[-dite-][?]' in the line before (10) is a struck-out word, likely 'disons'/'dite'; the sense is 'De façon plus intrinsèque, on a un hom.'.
In (12) the struck text is 'k.1_E', replaced by 't_E ⊗ F_1 = t_E ⊗_k 1_E'.
